newsitem.title: DENMARK: Carlsberg confident on EU probe.
newsitem.headline: Carlsberg confident on EU probe.

text.p: Danish brewer Carlsberg said on Monday that it believed a European Commission examination of its planned Nordic alliance with Coca Cola would rule in favour of the production and distribution deal.
"The partners believe that the agreement will be approved by the commission and hope for a speedy decision," a Carlsberg statement said, adding that there would be no further comment.
The Commission said on Friday that it had opened a full probe into a the proposed joint venture.

The European Union executive said in a statement that it wanted to address concerns that the venture, Coca-Cola Nordic Beverages A/S, could harm competition in the Danish and Swedish soft drink markets.

The venture would join the soft drink activities of U.S. soft drink giant Coca Cola and Danish brewery group Carlsberg, first in Denmark and Sweden and eventually in the whole of the Nordic and Baltic regions, the Commission said.
It also involves licence agreements and a distribution joint venture with the Swedish brewer Falcon, which is jointly owned by Carlsberg and the Finnish brewing company Sinebrychoff.

The Commission noted that the two parties held 60 percent of the Danish cola market, more than 40 percent of the Danish market for non-cola soft drinks and more than 70 percent of the Swedish cola market.
The Commission made a decision to open a detailed investigation after conducting a routine one-month probe into the venture. It now has four months to give a final ruling.
